source.title: One ticket to win them all: generalizing lottery ticket initializations across datasets and optimizers
source.authors: Ari S. Morcos; Hao-Nan Yu; Michela Paganini; Yuandong Tian

record.tranche_reason: Tests transfer of sparse initializations across datasets and optimizers using test accuracy, a different question and measure from the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports natural-label test accuracy for sparse winning tickets and random tickets. It does not test fitting random labels, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected models, adaptive-optimizer generalization gaps, large-batch penalties, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Most reported result values are presented in figures; the text describes selected comparisons but gives no exact accuracies.
record.test_reason: The study tests transferability of sparse winning-ticket initializations, a different claim from V1–V8. It cites the V2 original when discussing overparameterization but does not sweep width beyond interpolation. Its optimizer experiments compare ticket sources within each target optimizer, without establishing the adaptive-versus-SGD performance difference in V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that winning tickets from sufficiently large and diverse datasets contain partly generic inductive biases that transfer across natural-image datasets and optimizers. Transfer often approaches target-specific performance, while retaining some dataset dependence; transfer across domains and architecture topologies remains untested.
record.recipe_differences: Studies transfer of sparse winning-ticket initializations across datasets and optimizers, rather than the listed versions' interventions or measurements of generalization gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Source dataset size and number of classes affect transfer; pruning fraction changes outcomes; VGG19 and ResNet50 show different pruning behavior; target dataset and target optimizer vary.

fits_no_version.finding: Winning-ticket initializations transfer between CIFAR-10 halves; ResNet50 tickets beat random tickets at extreme pruning but underperform them at low pruning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transfer of sparse initializations between samples from one distribution depends on architecture and pruning fraction.

fits_no_version.finding: Tickets from larger, more complex datasets often approach target-specific ticket performance. CIFAR-100 tickets transfer better than CIFAR-10 tickets despite equal training-set sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse initialization transfer benefits from source-dataset size and class diversity.

fits_no_version.finding: Transferred VGG19 tickets outperform Fashion-MNIST-specific tickets at low pruning, where the latter overfit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transferred sparse initializations can reduce overfitting on a simpler target task.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG19 tickets transfer between Adam and momentum SGD, with SGD-to-Adam transfer below random tickets at low pruning and above them at high pruning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse initializations can transfer across optimizers, with benefits depending on pruning fraction.

record.problems: The central cross-dataset and optimizer comparisons are shown in figures without exact values in the text; the paper reports six random seeds and standard deviations. Results cover natural-image classification and fixed network topologies only.
record.rows_left_out: No additional row-level numerical outcomes could be extracted from the figure-only curves without reconstructing values. The paper's broad cross-dataset trends are represented by aggregate rows R4 and R5; detailed per-source and per-target curves appear in Figures 3 and 4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy alongside natural-label generalization.
Widening beyond zero training error; pruning fixed-topology networks does not establish this effect.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance under limited tuning and the effects of broader tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size effects and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on training-set size, strength, or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and comparisons with other measures.
Removal of highly memorized training examples versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because these rows measure a different construct, even where the ticket-transfer findings are clear. No claim-version verdict is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out accuracy comparison.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No comparison of adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers' generalization gaps; optimizer transfer concerns winning-ticket initializations.
No sharpness or other generalization measure analysis.

rows.subject: VGG19

rows.operation_detail: Trained CIFAR-10a winning-ticket initialization on CIFAR-10b and measured test accuracy at convergence.

rows.note: The text says CIFAR-10a tickets generalized well to CIFAR-10b; no exact accuracy is stated.
rows.check: Ticket transfer does not measure any listed version. The stated comparison baselines are a random ticket and a CIFAR-10b-specific ticket, rather than an unspecified baseline.
